mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has shown accelerating week-over-week declines (-11.1, -18.3, -34.6, -41.0), indicating strong negative momentum from habituated avoidance of non-essential trips. This momentum is expected to persist, producing a further mean decline in RETAIL_REC over the next 4 weeks relative to the last 4 weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC fell from -11.1 to -41.0 over four weeks with widening weekly deltas
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's weekly rate of decline shrinks or reverses (mean of next 4 weeks higher than last 4 weeks) despite continued negative momentum signal, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES mobility falls below -30 points, it indicates formal enforcement of work-from-home or closure policy, which cascades into reduced weekday commute-linked retail visits. Given WORKPLACES is now at -32.4, this threshold crossing predicts continued suppression of RETAIL_REC over the next 2 weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES declined to -32.4 at t-0w, crossing the -30 threshold
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC stabilizes or rises over the next 2 weeks even though WORKPLACES remains below -30, the threshold mechanism is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous rise in RESIDENTIAL (6.3 to 14.7) and decline in WORKPLACES (-10.9 to -32.4) jointly indicate deepening stay-at-home behavior beyond what either series shows alone. The interaction of rising home-dwelling and falling work mobility compounds to suppress RETAIL_REC more strongly than either trend individually, over the next 4 weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises and WORKPLACES falls concurrently for 2+ consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose each week while WORKPLACES fell each week over the last 4 weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's 4-week forward mean does not fall below its 4-week trailing mean despite continued joint RESIDENTIAL-up/WORKPLACES-down movement, the interaction hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has fallen sharply (-20.0 to -41.6), contrary to typical seasonal patterns where outdoor activity would offset indoor retail decline. In a regime of tightening restrictions during a low-mobility season, suppressed outdoor substitution behavior removes a buffer that normally supports nearby retail footfall, predicting a further near-term drop in RETAIL_REC within 1 week.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS declined from -20.0 to -41.6 over four weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises or stays flat over the next week despite continued PARKS decline, the seasonal substitution-removal mechanism fails.

mechanism_narrative: After RETAIL_REC falls below -40 for two consecutive weeks, historical base rates show partial mean-reversion as essential and pent-up demand resumes, even amid restrictions. This predicts a modest rebound in RETAIL_REC's 4-week forward mean relative to the extreme trailing decline.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC falls below -40 points for 2 consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC was -34.6 at t-1w and -41.0 at t-0w, both below -30 and nearing -40 threshold
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC continues to decline or stays flat for the next 4 weeks after crossing -40, the mean-reversion hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has turned negative (21.6 to -5.3) in tandem with falling TRANSIT (-0.9 to -31.9), indicating reduced trip-chaining where errands that previously bundled grocery and retail visits are being curtailed. This predicts a further short-term decline in RETAIL_REC within 1 week.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM fell from 21.6 to -5.3 while TRANSIT fell from -0.9 to -31.9
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises over the next week while GROCERY_PHARM and TRANSIT both continue to decline, the trip-chaining reduction mechanism is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: Joint sharp declines in TRANSIT (-0.9 to -31.9) and WORKPLACES (-10.9 to -32.4) together signal an enforced lockdown restricting non-essential travel, and their combined magnitude amplifies retail suppression beyond what either series predicts alone, over the next 2 weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 20 points week-on-week while WORKPLACES falls more than 15 points over the same period
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT dropped 14.8 points and WORKPLACES dropped 9.1 points between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's 2-week forward mean does not fall below its trailing mean despite both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES crossing their joint decline thresholds, the interaction hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM crossing from positive to negative baseline (21.6 to -5.3) marks the end of an initial panic-buying surge that had been compensating for broader shopping-category declines. Once this compensatory effect disappears, the overall retail-and-recreation average loses a prop and declines further over the next 4 weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM crosses from positive to negative values
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM moved from +21.6 at t-3w to -5.3 at t-0w, crossing zero between t-2w and t-1w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's 4-week forward mean rises above its trailing mean despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining negative, the compensatory-prop-removal hypothesis is rejected.
